svg.text: CHROMA lighting board — full build spec & technical design
Doc CHROMA-BRD-001 · rev A · DRAFT for engineering review · 2026-10-09 · owner: Andy England
Scope: a wifi-connected physical lighting console (8 group channels + master) that drives LIFX bulbs and WLED pixel fixtures (incl. 12 Playbill bars) through the CHROMA hub,
records performances against song position, and produces the dataset for training an AI to reproduce the operator's style.
Convention: ⚠ marks an assumption that must be verified against a datasheet or on the bench. Nothing here is bench-verified yet — prototype P0 (CHROMA-BRD-P0) gates this document.
1 SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE (solid = exists today · red dashed = new work)
FLASH press → full level on fast fixture
Safety: no software state may exceed per-fixture thermal/current limits
Photosensitivity: no flashing faster than 3 Hz by default
Standalone: board works with hub only (no internet)
3 FRONT PANEL — mechanical blueprint (top view, 1 mm = 2 px, origin top-left)
⚠ slot length and mount holes per chosen part; ch pitch 32
translucent cap, SK6812 behind; momentary NO
MX-style key switches (palette, bank, tap, cues, xport)
plate-mount; 3 mm plate OK for MX; shine-through caps
Rotary encoders w/ push (hue, sat, nudge)
EC11-class, 6 mm shaft; 28 mm knobs on E1,E2,E3
Toggles: art mode, who-drives, fader function
mini toggle; ⚠ confirm on-off-on contact map
⚠ viewing area vs module outline; bezel recess
bezel or light-pipe; driven from SK6812 chain
label tape in v1; OLEDs later
4 CHANNEL MODULE PCB (×8 identical + 1 master variant)
C1 100 nF · C2 10 µF · R2 1k + C3 100 nF
J1 PINOUT (2×5 shrouded IDC, ribbon ≤ 150 mm to main board)
fader wiper; RC filter (R2/C3) at module
analog ground, interleaved next to WIPER
filtered analog 3.3 V for the fader only
to MCP23017 input; active low, pull-up on main
to MCP23017 input; active low, pull-up on main
backlight power; 10 µF + 100 nF at entry
Master channel = same PCB, no ASSIGN switch, BLACKOUT wired separately.
Analog sections: keep WIPER away from PX data; AGND joins GND at one point on the main board (star).
Order 10 boards (8 + master + spare). 2-layer, 1.6 mm, ENIG optional. Fader mounting holes per ⚠ part.
D1 sits under the translucent FLASH cap; D2 lights the ASSIGN ring; both on the same SK6812 chain.
5 MAIN BOARD — pin map, expanders, power
ESP32-S3 PIN MAP (⚠ module-dependent: octal-PSRAM variants reserve GPIO35–37; avoid strapping pins 0, 3, 45, 46 and USB 19/20)
ADC1 works with wifi; ADC2 does not. Oversample ×16, EMA.
400 kHz; 4.7 kΩ pull-ups; ⚠ confirm bus load
keep in production for latency checks
populated only if P0 T1 fails; avoids a respin
MCP23017 ALLOCATION (I²C 0x20–0x22, inputs with pull-ups, interrupt on change)
bank A/B/C, TAP, REC, PLAY, STOP, BLACKOUT, toggles T1(2) T2(1) T3(2)
6 FIRMWARE DESIGN (ESP32-S3, Arduino-ESP32 on PlatformIO; ⚠ pin the core version)
9 ch × 16 samples → mean → EMA (α≈0.35) → 12-bit; deadband ±2 counts; endpoint cal
debounce 5 ms; long-press 500 ms (store palette, ASSIGN hold); encoder deltas via PCNT
wifi STA, power-save OFF, mDNS finds hub, WebSocket client, reconnect 0.5→5 s backoff
pack changed faders into one frame; button/encoder edges sent immediately
RMT drive of SK6812 chain; global brightness cap; state from hub 'ui' + local feedback
OLED: track, BPM, mode, bank, rec/sync state
if hub link lost > 10 s: backlights breathe amber; no output is stuck (hub owns state)
HTTP OTA over wifi; version in hello frame
WIRE PROTOCOL (WebSocket text frames, JSON; binary packing is a later optimization)
identify board; hub replies with ui
button down/up with board ms timestamp
labels, backlight colors, track, BPM, mode
Hub applies: bank → channel → group → parameter (level / hue / sat) → master → blackout → fixture output. The board never talks to a bulb directly.
7 HUB SOFTWARE DESIGN (extends hub/engine.py, server.py, scenes.py, layout.py)
Apple TV push, art → colors, LIFX output, AUTO painting; gains BOARD priority
Fixture / Group / Bank registry, capabilities, latency class (fast/slow)
existing LifxController behind a common push(fixture, color) interface
DDP sender per WLED node; segment mapping; frame pacing 60 Hz
/ws/board: protocol, mapping, master, blackout, flash, strobe limit (≤ 3 Hz)
event log + replay scheduler keyed to song position; overdub/replace/merge
ingest beat/bands/onsets from the Pi tap; align to song position
RECORDING FORMAT (JSON Lines, one file per take)
p = song position ms · w = wall clock ms · s = source control
g = group · k = parameter · v = value · a = audio feature frame
Replay clock: song position from Apple TV (⚠ pyatv position resolution and latency must be measured) interpolated with a local monotonic clock, resynced on each update;
user offset (nudge) applied on top. Takes: REPLACE a group's timeline, MERGE alongside, or OVERDUB. Last writer wins per (group, parameter).
8 LEARNING PIPELINE (so the AI eventually performs in your style)
Capture: board events + audio features + track metadata for every performance
Few-shot: Claude gets audio features of a new track + similar past takes → emits cue timeline
human rates it; accept rate tracked
Evaluate: replay AI vs human take; compare timing, color, group distribution
Model continuous curves (intensity, hue drift) from features; LLM keeps structure
Guardrails regardless of stage: output validated against fixture capabilities; flash/strobe limit enforced in the hub; per-fixture current and thermal limits are never AI-controllable.
Honest expectation: stage 1 can sound like your style on genres you've recorded fairly early; faithfully replicating your taste takes a lot of takes, and the dataset is the durable asset.
9 PLAYBILL BAR MODULE (12 frames of 5.5 × 8.5 in now; designed to grow)
SK6812 RGBW, ≈ 7 px, aimed ≈ 15° off vertical
light onto the print, ≤ 50 lux target
Nothing on the bar touches the frame; keep ≥ 25 mm clear.
Warm air from the bar rises toward the frame bottom. At
≤ 0.6 W/bar that should be negligible; confirm in S5.
140 × 216 mm (5.5 × 8.5 in); ⚠ confirm portrait/landscape and frame depth
≈ 120 mm long, centered under each frame; discrete bars, dark gap between
SK6812 RGBW, 60 px/m, ≈ 7 px per bar; RGBW for a clean warm white on paper
WLED max current 1.5 A for 12 bars (≈ 0.125 A/bar, ≈ 0.6 W/bar); typical use ≪ cap
listed Class 2 / LPS 5 V 3 A; 2 A fast-blow fuse at the source
60 °C NC bimetal thermostat in series with +5V on first and last bar (⚠ rating)
temp sensor on channel: dim at 40 °C, off at 45 °C; hub also limits level per fixture
JST-SM 3-pin both ends; trunk 20 AWG; data 24 AWG; inject +5V every 4 bars; 330 Ω + 74AHCT125 at start
wall screws/anchors; nothing adhered to the frame finish; ≥ 25 mm clear of wood and paper
target ≤ 50 lux at the print (⚠ measure); LEDs have negligible UV; hub can auto-dim idle
PETG/ASA brackets away from the heat path; metal channel is the heat spreader
new bar = connector + one WLED segment; add a node past ≈ 300 px or a second power zone
This is a design guideline, not a safety certification. Verify temperatures with a thermal camera at the cap for ≥ 2 h before leaving anything unattended near wood or paper.
10 BILL OF MATERIALS (rough; confirm every part before ordering)
avoid octal-PSRAM if GPIO35–37 needed; USB-C
⚠ pick part first; 60 mm alt. saves cost + panel
Playbill bars: SK6812 RGBW 60/m, channel + diffuser, JST-SM, brackets
5 V 3 A supply, 2 A fuse, 2 thermostats, wire
11 SYSTEM ACCEPTANCE TESTS (P0 tests T1–T8 carry over)
hold all keys, move all encoders
no missed edges; no wifi drops
heat the thermostat; kill the hub at 100%
LED power cut; no stuck output
script 10 Hz flashes from the board
bar + LIFX driven from one model
Software console in the GUI + recorder
Channel PCBs rev A + main PCB
own 2.4 GHz channel, AP close; coalescing
RC + oversample; DNP MCP3208 footprint reserved
slow class: washes only; fast effects on WLED
measure early; fall back to local clock + nudge
caps, backstops, thermal camera, low lux target
cardboard fit check before cutting metal

• Does the hub stay on the Mac, or move to an always-on box (Pi/NUC)? • Ethernet option for the console?
